name: Human Factors in Design - 2
description: This is the second of two sequential courses which provide an intermediate level review of the principles of human factors/ergonomics with an emphasis on design for inclusion. The course will introduce students to how human factors/ergonomics can be systematically considered and implemented in the human-technology-environment system with a focus on anthropometry, biomechanics and the design of work and workspaces. The course covers anthropometrics; biomechanics; work capacity evaluation; lifting and back injury; ergonomic seating and workspace; work-related musculoskeletal disorders; grasping; hand tool design; biological rhythms; human vibration; and design for disability and aging. Through lectures and course activities students will develop competencies in human factors and universal design for academic research and professional practice.
